subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In its upper course, a river mainly erodes:
options: Vertically, creating a steep V-shaped valley
questions.explain: Upper-course rivers erode downwards, forming V-shaped valleys and steep gradients.

options: A band of hard rock lies over softer rock that erodes faster
questions.explain: Differential erosion undercuts the hard rock, creating a waterfall and plunge pool.

options: A bend in a river, with erosion on the outside and deposition on the inside
questions.explain: Faster flow erodes the outer bank (river cliff); slower flow deposits on the inner bank (slip-off slope).

options: A meander neck is eroded through and later cut off by deposition
questions.explain: Erosion narrows the meander neck until the river breaks through, leaving an ox-bow lake.

questions.q: Which is a method of river transport?
questions.explain: River transport includes traction, saltation, suspension and solution.

questions.q: In its lower course, a river typically features:
questions.explain: Lower-course rivers deposit sediment, building floodplains and levees.

questions.q: Levees are natural embankments formed by:
options: Deposition of sediment along the river banks during floods
questions.explain: Floodwater deposits coarser sediment at the banks, building raised levees.

questions.q: Freeze-thaw weathering is a type of:
questions.explain: Water freezing and expanding in cracks breaks rock apart mechanically.

questions.q: Chemical weathering, such as carbonation, involves:
options: Rock being dissolved or chemically altered (e.g. limestone by acidic rain)
questions.explain: Carbonation dissolves limestone; chemical weathering alters rock composition.

questions.q: Which increases the risk of river flooding?
questions.explain: Intense or prolonged rain, impermeable surfaces and steep slopes raise flood risk.

questions.q: Urbanisation can increase flood risk because impermeable surfaces:
questions.explain: Concrete and tarmac reduce infiltration, so water reaches rivers faster.
Hard engineering uses built structures; soft engineering works with natural processes.

questions.q: Afforestation (planting trees) reduces flood risk by:
questions.explain: Trees intercept rain and their roots aid infiltration, reducing rapid runoff.

questions.q: A river landform with erosion on the outer bank and a sandy inner bank is best described as a:
questions.explain: The outer-bank erosion and inner-bank deposition are characteristic of a meander.

questions.q: To reduce flood damage cheaply and naturally, a council could:
options: Restore wetlands and use floodplain zoning
questions.explain: Soft engineering and land-use planning reduce risk sustainably.

questions.q: From source to mouth, a river's long profile generally becomes:
questions.explain: The long profile is steep in the upper course and gentler towards the mouth.
